changelog: Decision Procedure step 1: added a precise, narrow exception — when a continuation marker (-는데/-고/-아서/니까 etc.) is immediately followed by a discourse marker (그래서/근데/그런데/그러니까/그리고/아니/그래도/또) or a reporting verb (했더니/그러더라/물어봤더니/그랬더니) that opens a new independent clause, segment right before that marker instead of rejecting outright — targets the under-segmentation flagged by the critic without loosening the general continuation-marker ban.

Decision Procedure: added new step 2 explicitly stating that mid-utterance sentence-final punctuation ('.', '?', '!', '…') is a strong candidate split point exactly like end-of-text punctuation, so the model stops waiting for text-end before cutting — addresses the critic's under-segmentation cases involving internal '?' and quoted questions.

Examples — Segment: added 4 new generic examples demonstrating (a) split before 그래서/그런데 after a causal/continuative connective, (b) split after a quoted question before a reporting verb (물어봤더니), and (c) split at mid-utterance '?' marking a topic/option shift — reinforcing the new permissive Decision Procedure rules with concrete patterns, kept total at 12 examples.
